title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 46
paragraphs: To the Lydians whom he sent to test the Oracles he gave the following charge: from the day they set out from Sardis they were to count the days, and on the hundredth day they were to consult the Oracles, asking what Croesus, son of Alyattes, king of the Lydians, happened to be doing at that moment. Whatever each Oracle prophesied, they were to have written down and bring back to him. Now what the other Oracles prophesied is not reported by anyone; but at Delphi, as soon as the Lydians entered the sanctuary of the temple to consult the god and asked what they had been commanded to ask, the Pythian prophetess spoke thus in hexameter measure:

“I know the number of the sand and the measure of the ocean; I understand the dumb man, and I hear the speech of the speechless. There has come to my soul the smell of a hard-shelled tortoise boiling in a cauldron of bronze, with the flesh of a lamb mingled with it; bronze is laid beneath it, and bronze is cast over it as a covering.”
